title: Deuteronomy 1:19–33
context: Moses retells the events at Kadesh Barnea. The LORD had set the land before Israel and told them not to fear. The people asked to send spies, who brought back good fruit and a good report of the land, yet Israel refused to go up, accused God of hating them, and was terrified by reports of giants. Moses reminded them that God had fought for them and carried them like a son, but they still did not believe.

verses.text: We traveled from Horeb and went through all that great and terrible wilderness which you saw, by the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God commanded us; and we came to Kadesh Barnea.
verses.arminianNotes: Israel crossed the great and terrible wilderness, as God commanded, and reached Kadesh Barnea. God had brought them safely through every danger.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same evidence of God’s care. This is shared ground.

verses.text: I said to you, “You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God gives to us.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses tells them they have reached the land “which the LORD our God gives to us.” The gift is presented as already in hand.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise stress the certainty of the gift. This is shared ground.

verses.text: Behold, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up, take possession, as the LORD the God of your fathers has spoken to you. Don’t be afraid, neither be dismayed.”
verses.arminianNotes: Moses urges them to go up and take possession without fear or dismay. Faith means acting on God’s word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree that the command assumes the promise. This is shared ground.

verses.text: You came near to me, everyone of you, and said, “Let’s send men before us, that they may search the land for us, and bring back to us word of the way by which we must go up, and the cities to which we shall come.”
verses.arminianNotes: Here the people propose sending spies. Numbers 13:1–2 records God commanding the mission; the two accounts are usually read as complementary, with God approving the people’s request.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers hold the same harmonizing view. This is shared ground.

verses.text: The thing pleased me well. I took twelve of your men, one man for every tribe.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses approves and chooses twelve men, one per tribe. The plan itself was not sinful.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. The sin came later, in unbelief. This is shared ground.

verses.text: They turned and went up into the hill country, and came to the valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.
verses.arminianNotes: The spies go to the valley of Eshcol and explore the land. Moses compresses the story from Numbers 13.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers read the verse the same way. This is shared ground.

verses.text: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and brought us word again, and said, “It is a good land which the LORD our God gives to us.”
verses.arminianNotes: The spies bring fruit and say, “It is a good land which the LORD our God gives to us.” Moses highlights the good part of the report, which made Israel’s refusal less excusable.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same emphasis. This is shared ground.

verses.text: Yet you wouldn’t go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the LORD your God.
verses.arminianNotes: Yet Israel would not go up and rebelled against God’s command. Refusing to receive God’s gift is called rebellion.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree that unbelief is active disobedience, not mere hesitation. This is shared ground.

verses.text: You murmured in your tents, and said, “Because the LORD hated us, he has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.
verses.arminianNotes: In their tents they said God brought them out of Egypt because he hated them. Unbelief distorts God’s love into hatred.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see unbelief as slander against God’s character. This is shared ground.

verses.text: Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our heart melt, saying, ‘The people are greater and taller than we. The cities are great and fortified up to the sky. Moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there!’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: The spies’ words made their hearts melt: taller people, fortified cities, the Anakim. Fear was spread through words.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same power of discouraging speech. This is shared ground.

verses.text: Then I said to you, “Don’t be terrified. Don’t be afraid of them.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses told them not to be terrified or afraid. The command is pastoral as well as authoritative.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. This is shared ground.

verses.text: The LORD your God, who goes before you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
verses.arminianNotes: God goes before them and will fight for them, as he did in Egypt before their eyes. Past deliverance is the basis for present trust.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise ground faith in God’s past acts. This is shared ground.

verses.text: and in the wilderness where you have seen how that the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went, until you came to this place.”
verses.arminianNotes: God carried Israel in the wilderness “as a man carries his son.” The image is tender and personal. Arminian readers emphasize God’s fatherly love as the context of every command.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers also treasure the image of God’s fatherly care, which they see as grounding Israel’s adoption as his son (compare Exodus 4:22). This is shared ground.

verses.text: Yet in this thing you didn’t believe the LORD your God,
verses.arminianNotes: “Yet in this thing you didn’t believe the LORD your God.” Unbelief is named as the root problem.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Hebrews 3:19 makes the same diagnosis. This is shared ground.

verses.text: who went before you on the way, to seek out a place for you to pitch your tents in: in fire by night, to show you by what way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
verses.arminianNotes: God went before them in fire and cloud to find them places to camp. The guide they refused to trust had guided them every day.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same irony. This is shared ground.
